Subject: Private deployment: performance qualification & runbook (post-demo follow-up)

Hi Sam — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can get the Private deployment verified for production traffic. I pulled together the performance targets we discussed and a recommended measurement/runbook to validate the network path and streaming behavior.

High-level targets (we should confirm these are acceptable on your side):
- 95th percentile token-generation latency (end-to-end, client → model): <= 120 ms
- p99 tail latency budget (for streaming connections): <= 250 ms
- Sustained throughput target: 500 requests/sec (average sustained; burst to 1k for short periods)
- Concurrency (simultaneous open streaming sessions): target 80 concurrent sessions per deployment node
- Streaming tail-latency objective (for last-byte delivery on streaming responses): <= 300 ms
- TLS termination: recommended at NovaHealth edge (we can support mutual TLS to our side if needed)

Network/path expectations we need to validate:
- Private peering or VPN to the Redwood edge (we need single-hop private egress if possible)
- Consistent MTU across path (1500 preferred; let us know if you need jumbo frames)
- Jitter target: < 10 ms median; < 25 ms 95th
- Packet loss: < 0.1% for steady-state testing

Immediate asks from NovaHealth engineering:
1) Share a small topology diagram (edge routers, NATs, firewalls) — attached is an example topology (egress-topology-sample.png).
2) Run two short connectivity checks: traceroute to the redwood ingress (we'll provide IPs), and an iperf3 run for a 2-minute window (we'll coordinate times).
3) Confirm whether TLS is terminated at your edge or at a load balancer in your VPC. If terminated upstream, note the source IPs we should expect from your NAT.

Attachments: redwood-vpn-template.yaml (example config for a site-to-site VPN), egress-topology-sample.png

Proposed timeline:
- This week: share topology + procurement contact details (you mentioned procurement@novahealth.com).
- Wed/Thu: coordinate an iperf window and traceroute capture with your network team (we can be available 09:00–13:00 PT).
- Next Tue: run a short live streaming smoke test with a canary team once connectivity checks pass.

I tagged Marissa and Karthik for alignment on SLOs and runbook items. If you prefer, we can do a deeper network preflight call tomorrow.

Thanks — Connor

Connor / Marissa — adding a few engineering details so the runbook is actionable for NovaHealth:

Measurement plan (short):
- Pre-test: ensure clocks are NTP-synced on both endpoints. We'll use timestamps from our SDK to compute E2E token latencies.
- Traceroute + MTU: confirm no per-hop fragmentation; if any hop reports reduced MTU, request path MTU discovery check.
- Iperf3: run TCP and UDP streams for 120s. Request both 1) single long flow and 2) 100-parallel new-flow test to simulate connection churn.
- Packet capture: 30s at start, 30s steady-state, 30s at end — capture SYN/FIN and TLS handshakes.

Configuration tips (quick):
- Recommend enabling TCP keepalive at 30s for streaming sessions to avoid intermediate NAT idle timeouts.
- If using NAT gateways, ensure ephemeral port range is large enough (> 1024–65535); otherwise we hit source-port exhaustion under concurrency.
- For BGP/private peering: prefer advertising a /24 for peering. Ask NovaHealth to confirm BGP ASN for the peer.

Pass/fail criteria for run:
- p95 RTT <= 120 ms and no sustained packet loss > 0.2% during the 2-minute windows.
- Application-level streaming test: < 300 ms last-byte tail in 95% of sessions for the canary workload (we will provide a 10k-token synthetic prompt sequence).

I'll join Thursday's 10:00 PT session. Connor — can you share the ingress IPs and an iperf3 command we recommend? I'll also prepare a one-page test runbook we can send to Sam's network team.

Karthik
Sr. Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
